questions.text: What is the main representational benefit of multi-head attention over a single attention head?

options.A: It guarantees that every head learns a distinct grammatical rule.
options.B: It lets heads attend through different learned projection subspaces.
options.C: It removes the need to compute similarities between token positions.
options.D: It forces every head to share the same attention weight matrix.

questions.explanation: Different learned projections allow heads to form different attention patterns and combine complementary information; distinct specialization is not guaranteed.

questions.text: You replace 16 KV heads with 4 KV heads using grouped-query attention, keeping head dimension, sequence length, layers, batch size, and cache precision fixed. What happens to the stored KV-cache size?

options.A: It becomes one quarter of the original size.
options.B: It becomes one half of the original size.
options.C: It stays the same as the original size.
options.D: It becomes four times the original size.

questions.explanation: The stored cache scales with KV head count, so 4/16 gives one quarter of the original size.

questions.text:
For X.shape == (5, 12) and n_heads == 3, what shape does split_heads return?

```python
def split_heads(X, n_heads):
    n, d = X.shape
    d_head = d // n_heads
    return X.reshape(n, n_heads, d_head).transpose(1, 0, 2)
```
questions.explanation: The reshape produces (5,3,4), then transpose(1,0,2) swaps the first two axes to (3,5,4).
